finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: user-controlled query param 'f' is joined to /srv/files with filepath.Join, which cleans '..' segments but does not confine the result to root. An unauthenticated attacker can request f=../../etc/passwd and read arbitrary files readable by the process.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response written at files.go:18

trace.note: route /dl registered with no auth middleware
name taken directly from query param f
filepath.Join collapses .. so /srv/files + ../../etc/passwd => /etc/passwd; no prefix check
file contents returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No validation, no filepath.Base, no post-clean prefix check against root, no auth, no symlink resolution. Sibling handler avatar() uses filepath.Base (files.go:22), which is safe; download lacks it.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw query param f into filepath.Join(root, name) with no Base or prefix check. Join cleans "../../etc/passwd" to /etc/passwd, files.go:18 writes the contents back, and files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth, so an anonymous attacker can read any file the process can.
